messages:
maya.support: Hey team, customer (rachel@acme) opened a ticket — they're hitting errors when trying to stream the RERANK endpoint. They posted a curl that uses SSE / text/event-stream and get 415. Pasting their snippet and logs.

rachel.customer: We're trying to stream candidate scores as they arrive. Using:

```
curl -N -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"query":"fix login bug","candidates": ["change password","reset token"]}'
```

rachel.customer: We get HTTP/1.1 415 Unsupported Media Type and a JSON body: `{ "error": "unsupported content type for rerank; only application/json allowed" }`

sam.runtime: Rerank doesn't support streaming. It's synchronous: you POST candidates and get back scores. Streaming is only supported on chat/generate endpoints. The 415 is because of wrong Content-Type. We should tell the customer to use Content-Type: application/json. Also mention that some clients try `text/event-stream` to push partial candidates — not supported.

maya.support: Customer insists they need streaming because they have a long candidate list and want progressive scores to update UI. Any suggestions for a workaround?

alex.sre: If latency is the issue, try batching on client side (send chunks of candidates) or use a websocket proxy in front of Redwood to aggregate smaller rerank calls then stream results to client. But note that increases request count and cost. Also, we should verify server-side limits: payload size limit is 2MB and candidates limit is 1024 by default.

sam.runtime: Repro steps I used:

```
# BAD (streaming CT)
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"query":"x","candidates": ["a","b"]}'
# Response: 415 + {"error":"unsupported content type"}

# GOOD (non-streaming)
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query":"x","candidates": ["a","b"]}'
# Response: 200 + {"scores": [0.87, 0.12]}
```

sam.runtime: Note: we should make the error message 400+ more actionable: "rerank does not support streaming / use application/json or chunk candidates" — filing a small runtime ticket.

maya.support: Customer also reported weird score outputs (some negative scores), are those expected?

sam.runtime: Rerank returns raw logit-like scores by default for some models; we can return normalized probabilities if they want. Ask for request payload + model name. Also check if they accidentally passed `do_normalize: false` in their wrapper.

rachel.customer: We didn't set any flags, just the content-type. We'll try switching to application/json. Also please advise whether there's a recommended per-request candidate limit to avoid 413/timeout.

alex.sre: Recommend <= 512 candidates per request and <1.5MB body; for larger sets use chunked requests. Timeouts: the platform has a 60s default backend timeout for rerank; long lists may hit that.

incident-bot: ticket #INC-8921 created and assigned to eng-runtime. Priority: P2.

maya.support: Thanks. I'll relay workaround and ask them to try application/json + chunking. Sam — please add a small docs note and a runtime error message change request.

sam.runtime: Will do. Filed ENGRT-2417: return 400 with actionable message when Content-Type != application/json, and doc PR to rerank usage & candidate limits.

maya.support: Marking this thread resolved from support side, keeping eng loop open. :white_check_mark:

rachel.customer: Switching the content-type fixed the 415. We implemented chunking and the UI now shows progressive results via our websocket. Thanks!

maya.support: Closing ticket after confirmation. If anything else pops up reopen. :tada:
